q1_issues.issue: The event noun "destruction" is classed with the derived verb lemma `destroy` (and its witness named `sk_destroy_1`), but the naming rule permits inflection only and never derivation, so a deverbal noun must keep its own noun form.

q2_gaps: argument-bearing deverbal event nominalization ("the destruction of the greenhouse") — no rule states how the of-phrase argument attaches to the event-noun witness (thematic role vs the possessive of-genitive), nor confirms that such a noun keeps its own class symbol
notes: The causative frame is right: "cause" is an ordinary verbal event with Agent = the storm and the caused eventuality attached by Theme, per the causation-flavored-verbs rule. Mapping `destruction` onto `destroy` also pre-empts the downstream normalization the instruction set assigns elsewhere (welder to weld, go_out to fail).
